motion_surface_label: Example State official voter-information motion, animation, and interruption-safe fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes remain readable without non-essential motion, auto-advancing panels, or interruption-heavy live updates becoming the price of understanding the current answer.
reduced_motion_preference_note: Non-essential motion respects reduced-motion preference where practical, and the current answer remains available without motion-first presentation.
auto_moving_content_control_note: Automatically moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating components in the answer/help lane expose a visible pause, stop, hide, disable, or still/manual path when needed.
interaction_triggered_motion_note: Non-essential animation triggered by scrolling, hovering, focusing, filtering, or other interaction is reduced or suppressible rather than mandatory for comprehension.
stable_answer_lane_note: The current authoritative answer/help lane remains readable without racing rotating panels, shimmer placeholders, or repeated motion-driven layout shifts.
auto_update_and_interruption_note: Live updates do not silently replace or destabilize the answer while a voter is reading; a stable current summary remains visible.
countdown_timer_and_urgency_presentation: Countdowns, deadline reminders, and urgency cues remain understandable as stable text/labels and do not rely on pulsing or flipping motion alone.
carousel_marquee_and_rotating_notice_not: Carousels, rotating notices, or marquee-style components are paused by default or manually controllable when they affect the answer/help lane.
same_answer_across_motion_variants_note: Reduced-motion, paused, or static variants may change presentation but do not silently change the authoritative answer.
manual_help_contact_note: A plainly visible first-party help/contact lane remains available when the main route becomes unstable or distracting.
